reviews.verdict: The six documents mostly agree, but 24 seam problems remain: 1 blocker, 8 major and 15 minor, 14 of them on the thin-slice path. Most of the last two rounds' changes are consistent everywhere they appear: the route in cycle.json, the guidance class, the digest exclusions, the refreeze group, the D4 switch and setup order, the walled key, the product classes and admission returning a unit. The blocker: `vsdd feature route` must read a 'delta record' that has no path or class, and the specification lock refuses the architect's write during the delta step. The majors on the slice path: no record carries the method that the verdict's reviewer-ownership check needs; 'the cycle's base' is undefined, and cycle.json offers only `baseline`, a release tag; local delivery cannot merge into a branch checked out in the person's checkout; the wall rows deny builders the git status, diff and log calls that D4 approves, and a row with no `commands` key gets every git family; and state.md's 'whole key list' makes the [hooks] keys errors, which breaks D12. The other majors: 'live run' has two incompatible meanings, one story `method` key is asked to choose two stages' methods, and the core scope approves every configured command where D4 named only build and test.

The design keeps to every platform limit the probes established. No script reads a file or runs a command, nesting is one level, no step relies on the Agent tool, steps are held on their StructuredOutput call rather than a refused stop, spikes pass isolation themselves, hook timeouts are in seconds, and long commands re-attach inside the ten-minute cap. Three slice-path mechanisms rest on things that are untrue or unknown. Local delivery must merge into a branch the person's checkout holds, which git will not allow without touching that checkout. The fallbacks for the unproven caller-identity probes (27 to 29) identify a caller by its working directory, which is the shared project root for every story step. The slice plan also omits B8 and three other packages its own packages depend on. On coverage, four old capabilities are designed but cannot run as written: measured checks with no command or threshold key (clone fidelity, fuzz, coverage, perf budgets, cross-repo integration), test-writer methods no step can select (ui-tests, e2e-tests) along with orphan methods, notifications with no build package, and smaller gaps (stale mapping rows, Storybook setup, repo-initialization remote, sample-project downloads). Totals: 1 blocker, 5 major, 8 minor.

No blockers: 16 major and 9 minor findings, 9 of them on the thin-slice path. The happy path and most single failures inside a run are sound. A dead agent, an empty result, a compaction, a missing uv, a spike storm and a review that never converges all end in bounded agent starts. The agent-start budget matches the code: about 4 to 10 per story, 70 to 90 per realistic six-story wave. The design breaks where one run stops and the next begins:
- A lock orphaned in a live session is never released, and no command is named for it.
- A resumed parent cannot pass a child a story an earlier run admitted, so fast-route stories waiting on a merge decision never complete.
- A crashed planner run redoes everything.
- After a cap, the direct choice runs no round.
- A hand-edited approved spec leaves no decision and no command.
- An existing second clone never fetches state.
Two enforcement holes are on the slice path: delivery never checks red evidence, so a fabricated red gate bypasses tests-first; and in local mode git ref commands can move the integration branch past merge-guard. Local mode also has no defined merge that avoids the person's checkout. The tool cannot tell which method a stored review pass belonged to. Brownfield baseline comparison cannot be built for lint, format or scanner findings, or for a suite with no JUnit report at ingest.

Most of the user's decisions and requirements are built where blueprint 2.4 says: the model policy, the uv and standard-library hook runner, the walls, convergence, the three routine stops, the six spike entrances, compaction and warm start. The direct brownfield question is still not answered. None of the five starting points in blueprint 3.4 reliably reaches a release as written:
- An ingest can measure its baseline before its commands are known, and nothing measures it again.
- The hand-off of a queued request to feature is undefined, which affects the second-feature case and the import case.
- The no-tests, no-CI case branches its fix story before the harness exists, and it schedules a CI story in every later cycle because delivery.ci never leaves none.
- A hub of existing repositories cannot ingest its second repository.

Resume from cold is partly met:
- The survey runs long measurements with no job.
- Resumed feature, verify, maintain and wave runs lose the stories an earlier run admitted.
- A resumed standard-route feature holds no amendment.

The spike ledger is an unwalled channel out of the holdout wall. The person's quick spike opens with the wrong command form as the skeleton is written. On the slice path, local-mode delivery has nowhere to merge without touching the person's checkout, which the design promises it never does.

Totals: 10 major and 4 minor findings, no blocker.

The slice path can be built in outline, but not from the text as it stands. One gap stops it: the tool must recompute the review verdict before it merges, and it cannot. The rule counts a pass only when the stored agent type owns the pass's method, but no record stores the method. Nothing says how the tool finds the passes, disputes and rulings among the step records. The scoped review after a failed delivery overwrites the first review's records, because it reuses their names in the same run.

Local delivery, which the slice uses, merges onto a branch that is checked out in the person's own checkout. The design both requires that merge and forbids touching that checkout. The red and green gates leave open how a test maps to its file, where the base commit's report comes from, what a stub marker is, and whether a dirty worktree may be measured. That last gap lets green evidence be recorded for code that was never committed. The machine records and the tool's own outputs have no schema files, so packages the plan builds in parallel have nothing shared to agree on. The fixture the story tier starts from is named but not defined, and copying an overlay cannot mount a state branch.

The slice's package list in rewrite/STATE.md cannot be built in the order section 9 gives. It omits B6, C2 and B8, and needs S4 through H7. The sample project sits inside E1, which depends on almost every package. S3 is too large for one builder and has dependencies the table does not show, one of them circular. Five workflow packages miss agent packages that their universal tests need. Coverage of commands, agents, skills, workflows and rules is complete.

documents: rewrite/design/state.md 2.16 feature route row, 2.4 lock row
findings.problem: `vsdd feature route --run <id>` must derive the route from 'the delta record the step just wrote' or 'the stored change analysis', but no document gives that record a path, kind or class. The only candidate, an impact assessment under specs/architecture/assessments, is in spec-arch. That class is locked during the delta step: the latest spec decision is approved, and the run holds no amendment until `feature route` marks one. The route command is the step's closing command, so it runs before the step record exists. The story-writer, the spec packet and plan in delta scope also need the analysis, and the story-writer cannot read runs. Every feature run, and so every brownfield change and bug fix, has no input for its route.
findings.proposed_resolution: Add a file input: `vsdd feature route --run <id> --delta-file <path>`. The architect writes the delta data JSON in the temporary directory. The tool validates it and copies it into the cycle's tracked record (for example cycles/<cycle>/units/feature.json), which becomes the 'stored change analysis' that the story-writer, the packet and plan read. Update pipeline.md 2.9.4, blueprint 4.9, state.md 2.8 and 2.16, agents-skills.md 2.6 and the delta-analysis method.

findings.problem: The tool must count a review pass only when the stored agent type is 'the reviewer that owns the pass's method'. No record holds a method: the step identity is run, workflow, name, subject and attempt, and the hook stores only the agent type and the head. Step names are built at run time. In story.js they name the agent (review-adversary-p1); in wave.js they name neither the agent nor the method (integration-review-r1, security-r1). No document defines the step-name grammar the verdict function would need to find a unit's passes, fixes and arbitration. G3 cannot build the check or its conformance fixture as specified.
findings.proposed_resolution: Add `method`, and the pass or round number, to the step identity: brief() puts them in the echoed `step` object, pipeline.md 2.10.1 adds them to the schema, and the hook stores them. The verdict counts a record as a pass when its method is a review method of the perimeter (pipeline.md 2.9.13) and the stored agent type is the agent whose file lists that method. Fixes and arbitration are found by their methods. Update blueprint 4.10, hooks.md 2.11.7, state.md 2.8 and S7, and the packaging fixture.

findings.problem: A story branch is cut 'from the cycle's base', but cycle.json has no base, only `baseline` (a release tag, an ingest or an import; empty for a first release). The hotfix parenthesis makes `baseline` look like the intended source. Elsewhere the text speaks of a 'base branch', or branches.integration. Nothing says which commit is used (local or remote head, and when) or where it is recorded for the descent check. Read as `baseline`, feature-cycle stories are cut from the last release tag. The green diff then includes every earlier story of the cycle, and the red gate counts their passing tests as new and fails.
findings.proposed_resolution: Define the base once, in state.md 2.16 (the worktree library) and pipeline.md 2.9.1. It is the head of branches.integration (the remote head after a fetch in pr mode) when the worktree is created; in a hotfix cycle it is the release tag the cycle names. Record the commit in the run record and in the story closure. The unit's base, the descent check, the red-gate comparison and the green diff all use that recorded commit.

findings.problem: Local mode is one sentence: 'it merges locally'. With no remote, the integration branch is normally checked out in the person's main checkout. Git will not check it out again in .worktrees/_integration/. Advancing the ref leaves the person's index and files behind HEAD, and merging in the main checkout breaks the rule that 'the person's own checkout is never switched, pulled or committed to'. No behaviour is chosen, so G4a has no specified merge on the slice path.
findings.proposed_resolution: State the local-mode merge in pipeline.md 2.9.1 and state.md 2.16: merge in a tool-owned worktree on a detached head, and advance the ref only when the integration branch is not checked out elsewhere. When it is checked out, either fast-forward that checkout only if it is clean and at the old head (a stated exception), or return awaiting_merge with the one command for the person. vsdd doctor and status report the condition. Note the rule beside merge-guard.

documents: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.7 implementer and test-writer rows, commands key default, other row; 2.11.1 families; 2.11.10 core row
findings.problem: The implementer and test-writer rows grant only `git-commit`. `git status`, `diff` and `log` fall in `git-read`, so bash-git blocks the very calls D4 core approves, and smoke probe 7 (a builder runs git status) is blocked. An absent `commands` key means any family, so devops, the verifier, the technical-writer, the demo-recorder, the codebase-analyzer and the 'strictest' `other` row may push, open pull requests and add worktrees. agents-skills.md 2.9 says no pipeline agent does that. `git-read` also includes checkout, switch, fetch and gh api.
findings.proposed_resolution: Define git-read as the reading commands only (status, diff, log, show, rev-parse, ls-files, blame, grep) in hooks.md 2.11.1; a command in no family is refused unless the row holds '*'. Make an absent `commands` key mean ["git-read"]. Give every builder row ["git-commit", "git-read"] and the main row ["*"]. Mirror this in agents-skills.md 2.9.

findings.problem: step-results accepts a record only for a 'live run', and spec_locked is released while 'a live run' holds an amendment. Liveness is defined only for a lock holder (`seen` recent). discover, a report-only maintain and spike take no lock, so under that reading their step records are refused: the ideas checkpoint loses its score records, and a spike requested by one of their steps is refused at spike open. The other reading, 'not yet checkpointed', leaves the specification unlocked for 30 days after an amendment run crashes.
findings.proposed_resolution: Define it once in state.md 2.8. A run is live when its record has no checkpoint mark and either it holds the lock with a fresh `seen`, or its workflow takes no lock and it was opened within its time limit. Amendment runs always lock, so for spec_locked the definition reduces to lock liveness. Cite it in hooks.md 2.11.7 and blueprint 5.2 and 5.4.

findings.problem: D4 as adopted approves 'the project's configured build and test commands'. The core scope approves every configured command: lint, format_check, run (a product server), ui_check, docs_check, mutation, scan, audit (which may reach the network), bench, proofs, and every [[component]] command. 11.3 tells the person about only two adaptations, argument prefixes and workflow starts. This third widening sits inside core, although extended is kept off precisely because it goes beyond D4.
findings.proposed_resolution: Limit core to commands.build and commands.test (and those keys of [[component]]), matched as a prefix, in hooks.md 2.11.10 and blueprint 5.4. Move the other configured commands to extended. Alternatively, list the widening in 11.3 and in the setup explanation.

findings.problem: story.js and wave.js call `vsdd checkpoint <wf> --run <id> --subject <id>`, but the command is specified as `checkpoint <workflow> --run <id> [--outcome failed]`. A parser built to the table rejects the call, so the standalone story checkpoint fails: no closures are written, and the lock is held until the session ends or it goes stale.
findings.proposed_resolution: Remove --subject from both skeletons, because the run record holds the subject. Alternatively, add [--subject <id>] to blueprint 4.9, state.md 2.16 and pipeline.md S7, checked against the run record.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.11.2 review() and the delivery loop, 2.10.3
findings.problem: review() runs twice in one story run, once for the main loop and once after a delivery repair. Both runs name their steps review-<l>-p<k>, fix-<who>-p<k> and arbitrate, with pass starting at 1, so they produce the same step-record keys. Nothing says whether store_step overwrites or refuses. The verdict that delivery recomputes from the stored passes then mixes the two loops, or loses the converged pass.
findings.proposed_resolution: Prefix the scoped loop's step names with the delivery round (repair<n>-review-...). State in state.md 2.8 that a step record is never overwritten: a second write to an existing key is refused, so a collision fails in the harness.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.7 loop step 1, 2.10.8 Fix data, 2.11.1 converge(), 2.11.2 arbitrate
findings.problem: The arbiter is to be given 'the open findings and the builder's dispute notes', and the note 'is kept in the step record for the arbiter only'. But converge() drops the resolutions' notes, arbitrate(open) passes only the findings, and the arbiter cannot read runs. Under D18 it may dismiss only a disputed finding, yet it never sees the dispute.
findings.proposed_resolution: converge() keeps the notes of disputed resolutions by key and calls c.arbitrate(open, notes). The scripts put the notes inline in the arbitration prompt only; universal test 8 already keeps them from reviewers.

documents: rewrite/design/state.md 2.16 gate red row, 2.8 evidence lookup
findings.problem: A re-freeze record holds 'the new hashes of frozen tests the test-writer changed', and the evidence lookup returns it as the latest red record. tests-first and the green gate read the frozen set from that record. If it lists only the changed tests, the other frozen tests stop being frozen, and tests added in a coverage fix are frozen by neither record. The gate name in a re-freeze result is unstated, but fix() requires it to be 'red'.
findings.proposed_resolution: In state.md 2.16 and 2.8, state that a re-freeze record carries the complete frozen set (the earlier identities and hashes, the changed ones with new hashes, and the tests added in the fix pass) and that its result has gate: "red". Cite the rule in hooks.md 2.11.4.

findings.problem: The green gate requires that 'no stub marker remains', but no marker string, configuration key or method instruction defines one, and gates may not assume a toolchain. G2 must invent the check or hard-code a language idiom.
findings.proposed_resolution: Define a fixed token (for example VSDD-STUB in a comment) that the failing-tests method writes in every stub, and have the green gate search the story's diff for it. State it in pipeline.md 2.9.1, state.md 2.16 and the method.

findings.problem: The standard agent file has 'a six-key frontmatter' and 'Lint rejects any other key', and the example adversary file omits omitClaudeMd. Blueprint 4.3 and L-AGENT require omitClaudeMd: true on every agent, and spike-runner also carries isolation. An agent frame built from the template fails the lint, or a lint built from 2.7 refuses every agent file.
findings.proposed_resolution: In agents-skills.md 2.7, list seven keys (adding omitClaudeMd: true), plus isolation: worktree on spike-runner, and add the key to the example.

findings.problem: The spike command forms disagree. pipeline.md 2.8 writes `--step <workflow>/<subject>/<name>` without the attempt, which the prelude and state.md include. `spike record` is written without `--id` in 2.8 and 2.9.12. The spike workflow is said to open with `spike open --run <id>` and to call the shared runSpike(), which always passes --step, so spike open looks for an asking-step record that does not exist and refuses.
findings.proposed_resolution: Use the state.md 2.16 forms in pipeline.md 2.8 and 2.9.12 and blueprint 6. runSpike() omits --step when it is given no step key, and the spike workflow calls it without one.

findings.problem: Before any analysis, the feature survey must know amend (to run inside the open cycle), severity (a critical request bypasses the queue and is cut from the release tag) and intent. The documented survey options carry none of them; --amend appears in one sentence of state.md only.
findings.proposed_resolution: Add --amend, --intent <value> and --severity <value> to the survey signature in blueprint 4.9, state.md 2.16 and pipeline.md 5.1 S2.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 Details (story deliver bullet: local mode 'merges locally'), 3.6 (main-checkout sync row)
rewrite/design/state.md 2.3 (alternatives table), 2.12 [delivery] mode, 2.16 story deliver and release rows
findings.problem: In local mode the integration branch is the branch the person's main checkout has checked out (any repository with no remote, as in the slice and every new greenfield project). The design says only that the tool 'merges locally'. Git refuses to check that branch out in .worktrees/_integration/. Moving the ref with update-ref after a detached merge leaves the person's index and working tree at the old commit, so the checkout shows the story reversed as staged edits and the next commit from it reverts the story. Merging in the main checkout breaks the stated rule that the person's checkout is never touched. No rule chooses between these. vsdd release in local mode has the same gap.
findings.proposed_resolution: State one rule in pipeline.md 2.9.1, state.md 2.16 (story deliver, release) and blueprint 4.12. The tool makes the merge commit in a detached .worktrees/_integration/. When the person's checkout holds the integration branch and is clean, the tool fast-forwards it with git -C <root> merge --ff-only. When it is dirty, delivery returns awaiting_merge with the reason and the one finishing command. Record this as the single stated exception in the state.md 2.3 table and pipeline.md 3.6, and add a G4a fixture with the main checkout on the integration branch, clean and dirty.

documents: rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.9 (how the tool knows who is calling), 4.13 Liveness, section 10 items 27, 28, 29
rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.5 Ctx, 2.11.10 (caller markers, lifecycle-log, extended scope), 2.16
findings.problem: Story stages run as ordinary steps with no platform isolation, so the payload cwd of every test-writer, implementer, reviewer and clerk step is the project root, the same for every parallel story. A cd inside a command does not change it. Three fallbacks depend on a unique cwd. If item 27 fails, markers matched by process and cwd cannot tell concurrent steps apart. If item 28 fails, the lock is refreshed only by calls from a run-owned worktree, which no story step makes, and the main session makes no calls while Workflow runs; the lock then goes stale after 20 minutes mid-wave and a second session can take it over. If item 29 also fails, section 10 says 'item 27 must pass', so there is no fallback and the survey refuses every run. The extended scope's 'inside the caller's own worktree' has the same flaw for builders.
findings.proposed_resolution: In hooks.md 2.5, define the caller's worktree as the worktree holding the target path, or the directory of the cd, git -C or vsdd -C prefix, never the payload cwd alone. Use that definition in lifecycle-log, auto-allow and the marker fallback. Make any vsdd call carrying --run of the locked run refresh the lock (blueprint 4.13, state.md 2.11). Give items 27 and 29 a fallback that needs neither a rewrite nor a process walk: the hook keys the marker by a hash of the session id and the tokenised command, and the tool hashes its own argv and takes the newest unread match (the strictest when several match). Update the fallback cells of items 27 to 29.

findings.problem: Several measured checks have no command or threshold key. Nothing in the closed key list says how to run the clone-fidelity harness, a time-bounded fuzz target, the cross-repository integration suite, or a coverage measurement. There is no key for a coverage threshold, a performance budget or a regression percentage. documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.11.1 relay(); 2.11.2 story.js; 2.4 route row 'A run lock is held by a live run'; 5.1 need S2
rewrite/design/state.md 2.10 status --fix; 2.11 lock bullets; 2.16 vsdd lock release
findings.problem: Liveness is keyed on the session: any guarded call from the holder's session refreshes seen. Three ordinary events leave a lock held by a run that has stopped, inside a live session: relay() retrying a survey that already took the lock, a person interrupting a workflow, or a throw between the survey and try. The person's own calls keep that lock fresh forever. status --fix releases only a lock whose holder is dead, which is undefined for a live session; plain lock release has no stated semantics; the route says 'wait'. The survey is called idempotent in pipeline S2 but refused on re-entry in state 2.11.
findings.proposed_resolution: 1. Survey re-entry: a lock held by a run of the caller's own session, for the same workflow and subject, with no step record, is taken over. 2. Refresh seen only on calls that belong to the run (step.run on StructuredOutput, --run on vsdd calls, run worktrees), not on main-session calls. 3. Define lock release: own session or stale; --force (person) any; holder dead = stale or session ended. 4. The route and briefing name vsdd lock release when the holder is this session, else --force in a terminal. 5. Fixture: interrupt after the survey, re-run, and the run continues.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 tests and deliver rows, green-gate detail
rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.4 merge-guard and tests-first; 2.11.7 step-results; 2.10 row 6
findings.problem: Delivery requires green, verdict, demo and CI, and never red evidence. Green compares frozen tests with 'the latest red record' but does not need one to exist. step-results does not check gate entries against evidence records. A test-writer, which may write source before red, can commit tests plus implementation and return a fabricated passing red result; the implementer has nothing to write, green passes, and delivery merges. tests-first also ignores Bash writes to source. Blueprint 3.2's guarantee ('cannot merge code') is false.
findings.proposed_resolution: 1. gate green and story deliver require a passing red or re-freeze record for every kind with a red gate. 2. step-results checks each gates[] entry against the evidence record it names (gate, subject, sha, passed) and blocks a mismatch. 3. tests-first inspects Bash writes into source before red. 4. Cases for both.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 deliver detail (local mode); 3.6 'Nothing in 1.0 pulls or merges in the person's checkout'
findings.problem: In local mode the integration branch is usually the branch checked out in the person's main checkout. Git refuses to check it out in a tool-owned worktree. git update-ref leaves the person's index showing the story reversed, so their next commit undoes it. Merging in their checkout breaks the stated invariant and clobbers uncommitted work. The design defines neither path, and the slice's first local delivery hits this.
findings.proposed_resolution: Define the local merge: merge in the worktree where the branch is checked out when it has no tracked changes; return checkout_dirty (blocked, reason environment, naming the checkout) when it is dirty; when checked out nowhere, merge in a tool-owned detached worktree and move the ref. Amend the invariant wording. init and doctor report the case. Add slice tests for clean and dirty.

findings.problem: merge-guard does not match commands that move the integration or release ref without a checkout: git update-ref, branch -f/-M/-C, switch -C, checkout -B, fetch . x:<branch>. These fall in git-read ('every other git command'). The family table is wrong both ways: if git-read must be granted, test-writer and implementer (commands = [git-commit]) cannot run git status, diff or log; if it is implied, ref writes pass. Verifier and devops rows default to every family, including push, gh-pr and worktree, which agents-skills forbids. The tool never checks that the integration head is one it produced.
findings.proposed_resolution: Narrow git-read to read-only subcommands. Add a git-ref family that no agent holds, and have merge-guard block it for every caller when it names the integration or release branch. Every agent row lists commands explicitly, and an absent key means none; builders get git-commit and git-read. story deliver and gate wave refuse with integration_moved when the integration head is not one the tool recorded or produced through its own merges.

findings.problem: A review pass counts only when the stored agent type owns the pass's method, but the method is only in the prompt. Step records hold the identity, the agent type and the head. Step names follow no single pattern across story, wave and verify, and the step-name table was removed. The tool cannot map a record to a method, so G3 either rejects real passes or skips the check.
findings.proposed_resolution: Add method to the step identity: brief() puts it in the identity the agent echoes, and step-results stores it. The tool counts a record as a pass only when its method is a review method of that perimeter and the stored agent type owns it in the roster. Add a conformance fixture in which a builder echoes a reviewer's method.

findings.problem: A deterministic crash in a locked rule (step-results, gate-guard) blocks every step result or clerk call. The blocks reach step agents, not the person, who after two runs gets blocked/stuck with retry, direct and descope, none of which helps. Nothing names VSDD_FACTORY_HOOKS_QUARANTINE. A rule module's import error happens outside the per-rule try, so it is a runner crash, never logged as rule.error, and the quarantine condition cannot be met; only hooks=off remains.
findings.proposed_resolution: Import rule modules inside the per-rule try. The rule_error block's fix line names the restart command with the quarantine variable. The briefing and vsdd status list rules with repeated rule.error, with the restart line. The checkpoint copies a unit's last block codes into its blocked packet.

findings.problem: Every gate checks that a story is recorded in the run it is given, but admission is recorded only in the admitting run. When a fast-route story ends awaiting_merge (D15: the first CI story, any dependency change) or a run dies mid-child, the resumed feature run either skips story-draft and has no units, or reruns gate plan --story, which 'changes nothing', so the child's gates refuse. Fix stories from wave and verify are in the same position. The route loops with no progress.

Re-admission records the story in the calling run. feature passes the survey units to runStories() when story-draft is done. Scenario tests for a merge decision approved in a new session, and for a kill mid-child.

findings.problem: The done test counts a done step record 'inside a run that has not reached its checkpoint', without saying an earlier crashed run counts. Read as the current run, a resumed spec, ingest or plan redoes every planner step. If earlier records count, a resumed standard-route feature skips its delta step, so nothing marks the amendment and every evolve write is refused by the spec lock.
findings.proposed_resolution: Done records from any earlier run of the same workflow and unit that ended without a checkpoint count once they validate. The feature survey marks the amendment when the cycle's route is standard and it has no approved spec decision of its own. Fixtures: kill a spec run mid-way and resume; kill a standard feature after delta and resume.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.11.1 converge(); 2.11.2 story.js review() and unused u.guidance; 2.11.3 wave.js; 2.6 finding, revise and hold rows
findings.problem: After a cap, rounds_used is at least cap+1. On the next run converge() returns blocked/cap before any pass, with an empty open list, so direct does nothing and the same finding decision reopens. This is a regression of OPS-23. A waiver converges only if the tool's verdict applies settled waivers, which is unstated. The survey returns guidance, but no prompt carries it, so guidance from revise, hold, direct and blocked-direct never reaches an agent.

The tool's verdict applies settled waivers, so a waived unit's position is reviewed. brief() adds the person's guidance whenever present, with a universal test. Conformance fixtures for direct and waive after a cap.

Without a report, compare by exit status, announce that the check cannot fail while the baseline fails it, and schedule a readiness chore. Add a G2 fixture with a moved inherited finding.

findings.problem: 1. A suite with no JUnit report at ingest gives a baseline with no failing-test identities, so the harness chore and the first bug fix see every inherited failure as new. 2. pipeline asks for the harness only when there is 'no suite'; state also asks when there is 'no JUnit report'. 3. An inherited failing test that a story fixes stays inherited, so a later regression passes every gate.

Record whether identities were measured; when they were not, delivery of the harness chore re-measures them into the baseline, and that chore's own green gate requires only that the report is produced and its own tests pass. 2. One readiness condition everywhere: no suite or no JUnit report. 3. Closure records list inherited tests a story made pass, and gates stop treating those as inherited.

documents: rewrite/design/state.md 2.2 rule 6; 2.3 Push; 2.11 two machines and adoption; 2.9 State problems
findings.problem: Nothing fetches the state branch before the briefing or the survey. An existing second clone routes on stale state and redoes checkpointed work. Two machines can run the same wave at once, both build the same stories, and adoption lets one take over the other's open PR mid-delivery. Both reach conflicting closure-record pushes with no named repair.
findings.proposed_resolution: The survey fetches and fast-forwards, or rebases, the state branch before preconditions, and the briefing reports when state is behind the remote. The survey writes and pushes a lease (scope, run, machine, time); another machine's survey refuses while it is fresh; checkpoints and deliveries refresh it and the checkpoint clears it. A push conflict opens blocked, reason environment, and status --fix retries the rebase.

documents: rewrite/design/state.md 2.8 choice table, settling writes the record only
findings.problem: Settling open-spike writes only the decision record. It opens no named spike, carries no mission, and leaves the unit runnable. The step asks again, uses two more spikes and is blocked again. A later spike close is never fed back to the step.
findings.proposed_resolution: Settling open-spike also writes the named-spike request with the packet's questions, as spec-gap amend writes its request. The unit stays blocked on that spike, and the route names /vsdd-factory:spike open <n> -- <question>. spike close releases the unit, and the asking step receives the finding.

findings.problem: The built-in part of auto-allow requires a single segment, but the core prefix match of configured commands does not. A configured command followed by ;, &&, $(...), backticks, eval or sh -c with an opaque payload is approved without a prompt in the default permission mode, for exactly the commands the heuristic checks cannot read.
findings.proposed_resolution: Approve a configured command only as one segment followed by plain argument tokens: no separators, substitutions, eval, sh -c, xargs or redirects. shell.py marks commands with substitutions as opaque, and auto-allow never permits an opaque command. Add cases.

documents: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.1 secrets row; amendment 16; 2.7 builder rows
findings.problem: Builders keep outside readable, and the credential list misses ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/git/credentials, ~/.cargo/credentials.toml, ~/.pypirc, ~/.gem/credentials, ~/.kube/config, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.azure, ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json and ~/.gnupg. gh auth status --show-token prints the token, as gh auth token does.

documents: rewrite/design/state.md 2.9 Running line and driver instruction
findings.problem: The driver instruction follows only the Running line, which needs a live lock. A compaction just after a workflow returns, with the lock already released, drops it, and the driver stops.
findings.proposed_resolution: Print the driver line whenever driver.json names this session, with or without a live run.

documents: rewrite/design/state.md 2.11 liveness; 2.10 clearing is always safe
findings.problem: If step calls carry their own session ids (item 28), runs with no worktree (spec, plan, ingest, feature delta) refresh nothing, and their lock goes stale after 20 minutes. SessionEnd also fires on /clear and releases the lock whatever the reason, even if a workflow survives the clear.
findings.proposed_resolution: Also refresh on StructuredOutput with step.run equal to the locked run and on vsdd calls with --run. Probe whether a workflow survives /clear; if it does, keep the lock on SessionEnd with reason clear.

findings.problem: Whether the platform validates StructuredOutput before or after PreToolUse is unknown. If after, a done record can be stored for a result the platform rejects, which a later survey could count as done. The stated reason not to validate ('no stdlib validator') is contradicted by schema.py in the shared core.

findings.problem: Wave and release fixes always report fixed, so no finding can be disputed there. The arbiter can never dismiss one, and every finding upheld at the cap goes to a person, against D18's low-touch intent.
findings.proposed_resolution: A fix story's result carries the keys its fixer disputed, and the wave's fix() maps them to disputed. Add a harness scenario.

findings.problem: A clone whose 1.0 state branch exists but is not mounted is completely silent. Every model action there is ungated, and nothing says the project is a factory project.
findings.proposed_resolution: On SessionStart only, when a remote factory-artifacts ref exists (shell built-ins), print one line saying the state is not mounted, the gates are off, and to run setup. This extends D24's pre-1.0 exception without reopening D24.

findings.problem: The feature survey takes the lock before it writes or queues the request. A request typed in a second session during a wave is refused and lost.
findings.proposed_resolution: When another cycle is active and the request is not critical, write requests/CR-NNN.md and return queued before trying the lock.

documents: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.1 bash-destructive; 2.7 devops and verifier rows
findings.problem: Recursive deletion of worktree directories is allowed, and git worktree remove --force is blocked only outside the worktree roots. A builder can destroy a sibling story's or a named spike's uncommitted work.
findings.proposed_resolution: Allow recursive deletion only of build output inside the caller's own worktree; only the tool removes worktree directories. Add a sibling-worktree case.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.3 feature row, 2.4 route row 'No cycle is open and a change request is queued', 2.9.4 survey row, 2.9.7 close row
rewrite/design/state.md 2.5 change request row, 2.7 next field, 2.11 lock, 2.16 survey row
findings.problem: The route names 'feature with the oldest queued request', but nothing defines what next.args carries, and the feature survey can receive a request only as free text in --request-uri, which always writes a new request file. There are three readings and all fail. The request text duplicates the request and leaves the CR queued, so it is offered again after the release. 'CR-NNN' is stored as a new request whose text is the identifier. An empty args fails because request is required on a first run. Whether a request typed while another run holds the lock is recorded before the lock refusal is also unstated.
findings.proposed_resolution: Define next for a queued request as {command: '/vsdd-factory:feature', args: {request: 'CR-NNN'}}. A request argument that is exactly a queued CR id is passed as --subject and activates that file instead of writing a new one. feature with no request and no amend takes the in-flight request, or else the oldest queued one. The survey writes a new request file before any lock check and returns 'queued' without taking the lock when a cycle is active. Apply this in pipeline 2.3, 2.4 and 2.9.4, state 2.5, 2.7 and 2.16, and blueprint 4.9, and add a fixture for a typed request that is queued and later activated once.

documents: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 'Where a child's unit comes from', 2.9.4 story-draft and deliver rows, 2.9.5 readiness paragraph
rewrite/design/state.md 2.12 missing-commands bullets, 2.16 gate plan row, 2.8 cycle record (no base field)
findings.problem: On a fast route the story-writer writes and admits the readiness chores and the change's own story in one step. Admission cuts every branch at once from 'the cycle's base', which is not defined anywhere. The fix story's worktree therefore lacks the test harness that the readiness chore later delivers, and it is never refreshed, because delivery rebases only on a conflict. Its red gate cannot produce a JUnit report, so the story is blocked and then stuck. On the standard route, plan schedule puts only the scaffold alone in the first wave, so a harness chore can share wave 1 with stories whose red gate needs it.

When the route lists readiness stories, the fast route runs story-draft and deliver twice: first the readiness chores alone, then the change's own stories. plan schedule puts the test-harness chore in a first wave of its own, like the scaffold. Apply this in pipeline 2.9.1, 2.9.4 and 2.9.5, state 2.12 and 2.16, and blueprint 4.6, and add an E4 assertion that the fix story's red gate reads a JUnit report.

findings.problem: The design maps multi-repository brownfield to 'ingest with repo for each repository', but the second ingest fails at several points. Its done test reads the first ingest's closed ingest.json, so every stage reads as done. Its baseline would overwrite the first one's, and its decision would reuse the identifier spec in _standing. Once the first baseline is approved, the whole-set specification lock refuses its writes, because an ingest holds no amendment. The route never names it, since a baseline already exists. The gates compare against one baseline measured with one repository's commands, and toolchain.toml cannot fill per-repository commands. Which run opens the hub's single release decision is also unstated.
findings.proposed_resolution: In a hub, ingest without repo covers every member in one run, storing one baseline object per repository in the ingest closure (each with its own integration head and measurements, read by the gates for stories with that repo). It writes toolchain.toml with a [[repo]] section per member, whose approval fills that entry's unset commands, and it ends at one spec decision. A member added later is ingested with repo in a run that holds an amendment. The route's ingest row becomes 'a member has no baseline'. In a hub, verify runs once at the hub and opens the one release decision. Apply this in pipeline 2.4, 2.9.8, 2.9.11 and 3.2, state 2.5, 2.8 and 2.14, and blueprint 3.4 and 4.13, and have E4 run (4) ingest two existing repositories.

findings.problem: Admission records a story only in the run that admitted it, and every gate refuses a story not recorded in the run it is given. A new run of the same feature command (after the session ended mid-review) re-runs story-writer, and gate plan --story 'changes nothing', so the story is not recorded in the new run and its gates refuse it (blocked, then stuck). If the earlier run checkpointed, story-draft is closed and skipped, and the feature survey returns no units, so the new run has nothing to deliver. Fix stories admitted by earlier verify, maintain or wave rounds are in the same position, since fix stories are not in the plan's wave map.
findings.proposed_resolution: The survey of every workflow that calls story returns, as units, every story the open cycle admitted for that workflow (and a wave's fix stories) that is not delivered, and records each in the new run. gate plan --story, re-run for a story an earlier run admitted, records it in this run and returns the unit. When story-draft is done, the feature deliver stage takes its units from the survey. Apply this in pipeline 2.9.1, 2.9.4 and 2.10.8 and state 2.8 and 2.16, with a harness scenario that kills a fast route after admission. The standalone story survey on the slice path must likewise record its unit in its own run.

The question and the runner's answer are written into the project ledger in .factory/spikes/, which test-writers, implementers, the story-writer and the architect may read. findings.problem: In local mode (no remote) the integration branch is normally the branch checked out in the person's main checkout, because init reads the current branch names. Git will not check out the same branch in the tool's _integration worktree. Merging in the person's checkout breaks the stated rule and fails or mixes changes when that checkout is dirty. Moving the ref from elsewhere leaves the person's index and files out of step with their HEAD. The design picks neither, so the G4a builder must break a promise either way. The slice delivers in local mode.
findings.proposed_resolution: In local mode the integration branch is checked out only in .worktrees/_integration/, and story deliver merges there with git hooks running. vsdd init detects a person's checkout on that branch, setup offers the one command that moves it to another branch, and doctor reports it. Otherwise story deliver returns refused with that reason. Apply this in pipeline 2.9.1, state 2.12 and 2.16, hooks 2.11.4 and blueprint 4.12, and leave the slice sample's main checkout on a non-integration branch.

findings.problem: runSpike() always opens with 'spike open --run <id> --step <stepKey>', while the spike workflow (the person's entrance) must open with --run alone and read the question from the run record. Ported as written, the person's quick spike passes an empty or invented step key and is refused. hooks.md's 'Who asked' row names only the step record and the admission, so the H8 and S6 builders read different rules.
findings.proposed_resolution: runSpike() omits --step when the step key is empty, and the spike workflow calls it that way. hooks.md 2.11.6 adds the third source: the run record of a spike run, whose asker is the main session.

findings.problem: Three texts remove spike worktrees older than 14 days, keeping only the branch of an open named spike. Only the configuration comment says 'finished'. A named spike spans many sessions, and its worktree holds .spike/STATE.md, .spike/TASKS.md and any hand-made work, so checkpoint or status --fix deletes it on day 15 while the spike is still open. Attaching is not said to recreate it.
findings.proposed_resolution: Count retention from the entry's verdict, or from delivery of the asking unit, and never remove an open named spike's worktree. Use the same wording in blueprint 6, pipeline 2.8 and state 2.10, 2.12 and 2.17.

findings.problem:
The tool must count a pass only when the stored agent type owns the pass's method. The step identity (run, workflow, name, subject, attempt) and the step record carry no method, so that rule cannot be applied.

Nothing defines how the verdict function rebuilds converge()'s inputs from step records: which records are passes, the items each pass had to account for, disputes, rulings, waivers and the cap.

findings.problem: Local mode 'merges locally' onto the integration branch, which is normally checked out in the person's checkout. Merging there touches that checkout, which state.md 1 and pipeline 3.6 forbid. Moving the branch elsewhere with update-ref leaves the person's index and tree stale.
findings.proposed_resolution:
Specify the mechanism once:
1. Make the merge commit in the detached integration worktree.
2. Move the branch with update-ref <new> <old>.
3. If the branch is checked out in a clean person's checkout, run 'git -C <root> merge --ff-only' as the one stated, announced exception.
4. If that checkout is dirty, return awaiting_merge with 'commit or stash, then rerun'.
State this in pipeline 2.9.1 and state.md 2.16, and refer to it from G4a and state.md 1/2.3.

findings.problem:
On the second return, the hook stores still-ungrounded findings as grounded:false (advisory). The script receives the agent's unmarked copy, so judge() treats them as blocking.

The script then loops fix rounds and may end blocked at the cap. Meanwhile the tool's stored verdict is converged, so the checkpoint opens no decision and the story is stuck until the next run. The conformance fixtures cannot catch this, because grounding exists only in Python.
findings.proposed_resolution:
- On the second return, have step-results return updatedInput for the StructuredOutput call, marking the ungrounded findings grounded:false.
- Make judge() and its Python copy treat grounded===false as not hard.
- Add a conformance fixture, and add the StructuredOutput rewrite to probe 27.
- Fallback if updatedInput is not honoured: block until the reviewer drops the finding or lowers it to low.

findings.problem:
Six facts the gates and the hook depend on are undefined:
1. How a JUnit test case maps to its file (the file attribute is optional).
2. Where the base commit's report comes from.
3. How green-by-design and wiring exemptions are marked.
4. What a stub marker is.
5. Assertion failure versus build error. A Python stub that raises NotImplementedError is a JUnit error, so the slice's sample story would fail the red gate twice.
6. How a criterion links to its tests for the demo table.
G2 and H5 would each invent answers, and the answers need not agree.
findings.proposed_resolution:
Add a gate-inputs list to pipeline 2.9.1, mirrored in state.md 2.16, with the agent-side half in the failing-tests method:
1. Test identity is classname plus name. The file is the file attribute, else the classname mapped through the tests globs (init and doctor warn when neither exists).
2. The base report is measured once in a temporary detached worktree and cached as evidence keyed by the base sha.
3. A failure is <failure>, or an <error> of a constant list of not-implemented types; any other error fails the gate.
4. The stub marker is the fixed string VSDD-STUB.
5. A test is exempt when its name contains wiring or green_by_design.
6. Test names carry ac<N>, and the red record keeps the criterion-to-test map that gate demo uses.

findings.problem:
Gates bind evidence to the head commit but run the commands in the worktree as it stands. No rule covers uncommitted changes.

Uncommitted passing code can therefore earn green evidence for a head that fails, and delivery merges that head. Conversely, after an uncommitted edit, a gate run again on the same commit returns the old cached result.
findings.proposed_resolution: State that every story gate refuses a dirty worktree. Ignored files and untracked files under the report path do not count. The refusal is passed:false with the failure 'uncommitted changes: commit, then rerun'. Write this in pipeline 2.9.1 and state.md 2.16, and add a G2 fixture.

findings.problem:
state.md 2.8 says the record field lists are the pipeline's schemas, but pipeline 2.10 defines only result schemas. The run, closure, decision, cycle, evidence and job records have no schema, and C1 delivers none.

The red record's frozen-test list, the patch-id field and the run record's story list are therefore not settled. Yet S2a, S2b, S3, G2, G3, G4a, H5 and H7 are built in parallel against them.
findings.proposed_resolution: Have C1 also write run, closure, decision, cycle and evidence schemas, taken from the state.md 2.8 field lists. The evidence schema includes red frozen entries {id, file, sha256}, patch_id, sha and passed. state.md 2.8 then cites those files.

findings.problem:
The survey, close and delivery output schemas are given as field lists only, with no required list and no JSON. The tool prints a short error object, and relay's fallback is {ok:false, error}.

If C1 requires every field, as the rule 'scripts read only required fields' implies, the clerk cannot return errors without inventing values. If C1 requires only ok, story.js reads non-required fields, against 4.10.
findings.proposed_resolution:
- State that every tool output prints every field of its schema, with empty values on error, so all fields can be required.
- Give relay() a fallback built from the schema: {...emptyOf(schema), ok:false, error}.
- Write the survey, close and delivery schemas as JSON in 2.10.

findings.problem:
A non-isolated workflow step starts every Bash call in the project root, so a builder commits with 'cd <worktree> && git commit' or 'git -C'. The payload's cwd is therefore the main checkout, which in local mode has the integration branch checked out.

Read literally, merge-guard ('while the integration branch is checked out') then blocks every builder commit. Liveness by 'cwd inside a worktree the run owns', the fallback for probe 28, never fires for steps.
findings.proposed_resolution:
- Define the effective directory of a Bash call in hooks.md 2.5: the last cd target or git -C path, else cwd. Use it for ctx.story, merge-guard, auto-allow's worktree tests and liveness; liveness also uses target for file tools.
- Add two cases: 'cd <worktree> && git commit' with the main checkout on the integration branch is allowed; 'git commit' in the main checkout is blocked.

findings.problem:
agents-skills 2.9 says the implementer reports a wrong frozen test under test_defects and 'the workflow sends it to test-writer'. story.js gives the implement step no data schema, never reads test_defects, and has no route to the test-writer before review.

A wrong frozen test therefore blocks with kind gate, and becomes a stuck decision after two runs.

- Give the implement step a data schema that requires test_defects (key, path, reason).
- When the result is not green and test_defects is non-empty, run one test-writer test-fixes step ending with gate red --refreeze, then the implement step once more.
- State this in pipeline 2.9.1, and add a harness scenario.

findings.problem: An updatedInput with no permissionDecision flows through normal permission evaluation of the rewritten command, which begins 'VSDD_CALLER=...'. A static allow rule such as Bash(vsdd:*) will not match it, so the D4 static-rule fallback would prompt on every vsdd call not permitted by auto-allow.
findings.proposed_resolution:
- Add to probe 27 a check that a static allow rule still approves the rewritten command.
- If it does not, have auto-allow return Permit with updatedInput for every vsdd call the caller's row grants.

findings.problem: Simplification. The runner already rewrites every vsdd command, yet it also writes a one-time marker file that the tool reads and deletes. It could put the caller facts in the prefix directly, with the same forgery protection (gate-guard blocks typed VSDD_* assignments, and the prefix is added after the rules) and the same hooks-alive test.
findings.proposed_resolution: Prefix VSDD_CALLER_SESSION, VSDD_CALLER_AGENT, VSDD_CALLER_TYPE and VSDD_CALLER_CWD, quoted, instead of a marker key. This saves one record type, key generation, marker pruning and the read-delete race.

findings.problem: Simplification. The merge guard needs one fact: the latest pass by its owning reviewers, at the head's patch-id, covered every item and left no blocking finding beyond arbiter dismissals (after a dispute) and waivers. Re-running a full Python port of converge() over every stored record is more than that fact needs.
findings.proposed_resolution: Define the tool's verdict as judge() in Python applied to the last pass, minus dismissals (the arbitrate record checked against fix-record disputes) and waivers, with rounds_used counted as the passes stored. This drops the Python converge() port, about half the conformance fixtures and most of P3BLD-01's reconstruction, while keeping every enforcement.
